How could he drown, when You are the most just of judges? He said, ‘O Noah, indeed he is not of your family.’ That is, those whom I promised to save, because I only promised you the salvation of those of your family who believed. That is why He said, And your family, except for those of them against whom the word has already passed. So this son was among those against whom the word of drowning had already passed, because of his disbelief and opposition to his father, the Prophet of God, Noah, peace be upon him. More than one of the imams has stated that whoever interpreted this to mean that he was not his son, but rather the son of fornication was mistaken. The statement that he was not his son, but rather the son of his wife, is narrated from Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Ubayd ibn Umair, Abu Ja`far Al-Baqir, and Ibn Jarir. Some of them used as evidence his statement, It is an unrighteous deed, and his statement, So they betrayed them. Among those who said this, Al-Hasan Al-Basri used as evidence these two. The two verses, and some of them say his wife’s son. This may mean that he meant what Al-Hasan meant, or he meant that it was attributed to him metaphorically because he was his foster son. And God knows best. Ibn Abbas and more than one of the Salaf said: No Prophet’s wife ever committed adultery. He said: And his saying: He is not of your family means those whose salvation you were promised. And Ibn Abbas’s saying in this is the truth that cannot be avoided, for God, the Exalted, is too jealous to allow a Prophet’s wife to commit fornication. For this reason God became angry with those who accused the Mother of the Believers, Aisha, the daughter of As-Siddiq, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and denounced the believers who spoke of this and spread it. For this reason God, the Exalted, said: “Indeed, those who came with the slander are a group among you. Do not think it is evil for you; rather, it is good for you. To each person among them is what he has earned of sin, and he among them who took upon himself the greater part thereof will have a great punishment. * Why did not, when you heard it, the believing men and believing women think well of one another and say, “This is a manifest slander?” * Why did they not produce four witnesses for it? But since they did not produce witnesses, then those are the liars in the sight of God. * And were it not for God’s favor upon you and His mercy in this world and the Hereafter, a great punishment would have afflicted you for what you uttered therein, * When you were receiving it with your tongues and saying with your mouths that of which you had no knowledge.” And you think it is insignificant, but it is grave in the sight of God.” Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada and others, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: He is his son, except that he differed with him in action and intention. Ikrimah said in some letters that he did an unrighteous deed, and betrayal is not done in a way that is not appropriate. It was mentioned in the hadith that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it thus, so Imam Ahmad said: Yazid bin Harun told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Asma bint Yazid, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recite: Indeed, it is an unrighteous deed. And I heard him say: “O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God. Indeed, God forgives all sins.” And He does not care. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Most Merciful. Ahmad also said: Waki’ told us, Harun al-Nahwi told us, on the authority of Thabit al-Banani, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Umm Salamah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it: Indeed, it is an unrighteous deed. Ahmad also repeated it in his Musnad. Umm Salamah is the Mother of the Believers, and it appears, and God knows best, that she is Asma bint Yazid, for she is also called by that name. Abdul Razzaq also said: Al-Thawri informed us on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah on the authority of Musa bin Abi Aishah on the authority of Sulayman bin Qubbah who said: I heard Ibn Abbas asked while he was next to the Kaaba about the statement of God: And they both betrayed them. He said: It was not for adultery, but this one was telling people that he was crazy, and this one was pointing out the guests. Then he recited: Indeed, it is an unrighteous deed. Ibn Uyaynah said: Ammar Al-Dahni informed me that he asked Saeed bin Jubair about that and he said: He was the son of Noah. God does not lie. God the Almighty said: And Noah called to his son. Some scholars said: No prophet’s wife ever committed adultery. This was also narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ad-Dahhak, Maymun bin Mihran, and Thabit bin Al-Hajjaj. This is the choice of Abu Ja`far bin Jarir and it is the correct one, about which there is no doubt.
11:48: God Almighty tells us about what was said to Noah, peace be upon him, when the ship landed on Judi, peace be upon him and upon the believers with him and upon every believer from his descendants until the Day of Resurrection, as Muhammad bin Kaab said: Every believing man and woman entered into this peace until the Day of Resurrection, and likewise every unbeliever, man and woman, entered into the torment and enjoyment until the Day of Resurrection. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: When God wanted to stop the flood, He sent a wind over the face of the earth, so the water stopped and the springs of the earth, the great abyss and the gates of heaven were blocked. God Almighty says: And it was said, O earth, swallow your water verse, so the water began to decrease, diminish and retreat. The ark settled on Judi, as the people of the Torah claim, in the seventh month, seventeen nights had passed from it, on the first day of the tenth month, he saw the tops of the mountains. When forty days had passed after that, Noah opened the window of the ark in which he had boarded, then he sent the raven to see what the water had done, but it did not return to him. So he sent the dove, and it returned to him, but it did not find a place for its feet, so he stretched out his hand to the dove and took it. Then he brought it in, and seven days passed, then he sent it to look for him, and it returned when evening came, and in its mouth were olive leaves, so Noah knew that the water had subsided from the face of the earth. Then he remained seven days, then he sent it out, but it did not return, so Noah knew that the earth had appeared. When the year was completed between when God sent the flood and when Noah sent the dove, and one day of the first month of the year two entered, the face of the earth appeared and the land appeared, and Noah removed the covering of the ark. In the second month of the year two, in twenty-six nights of it, “It was said, ‘O Noah, disembark in peace from Us’” verse.
11:49: God Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, this story and similar ones: Of the report of the unseen meaning of the report of the past unseen, We reveal it to you as if you were witnessing it. We reveal it to you, meaning We teach you about it as a revelation from Us to you. You did not know it, nor did your people, before this. That is, neither you nor any of your people had knowledge of it, so that those who deny you could say that you learned it from them. Rather, God informed you of it in accordance with what was the correct matter, as the books of the prophets before you testify. So be patient with the denial of those from your people who deny you and their harm to you, for We will support you and surround you with Our care and make the outcome for you and your followers in this world and the hereafter, as We did with the messengers when We supported them against their enemies. Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe. The verse. God Almighty also says: “And Our word has already gone forth for Our servants, the messengers. Indeed, they will be the ones who are aided.” The verse. God Almighty also says: “So be patient. Indeed, the outcome is for the righteous.”
11:50: God Almighty says, And We sent to Aad their brother Hud commanding them to worship God alone, with no partner for Him, forbidding them from the idols that they invented and for which they invented names of gods, and he informed them that he did not want any reward from them for this advice and message from God, but rather he sought his reward from God who created him. Do you not understand? He calls you to what is good for you in this world and the hereafter without a reward. Then He commanded them to seek forgiveness, which expiates past sins, and to repent for what they will face. Whoever has this characteristic, God will make his provision easy for him, make his affairs easy for him, and protect his status. For this reason He said: He will send down upon you abundant rain from the sky. And in the hadith, Whoever adheres to seeking forgiveness, God will make for him a way out of every distress and a way out of every difficulty, and will provide for him from where he does not expect.

11:53: God Almighty tells us that they said to their prophet, You have not brought us any clear proof, meaning an argument and evidence for what you claim, nor will we abandon our gods because of your word, meaning simply because you say, Leave them, we will abandon them. Nor will we believe you, believing that they said, We only say that some of our gods have afflicted you with evil, meaning, We think only that some of the gods have afflicted you with madness and insanity in your mind because of your prohibition of worshipping them and your criticism of them. He said, Indeed, I call God to witness, and you bear witness, that I am innocent of what you associate * besides Him, meaning, I am innocent of all rivals and idols. So plot against me all together, meaning, you and your gods, if it is true. Then do not respite, meaning, the blink of an eye. And His statement, "Indeed, I have put my trust in God, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds it by the forelock," meaning, under His power and authority, and He is the just ruler who does not transgress in His judgment, for He is on the straight path. Al-Walid bin Muslim said on the authority of Safwan bin Amr on the authority of Aifa bin Abdul Kila’i that he said regarding the words of God Almighty: “There is no creature but that He holds it by its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path.” He said: He holds the forelocks of His servants and teaches the believer until he is more compassionate towards him than a father is towards his son and says: What has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous? This position contains a conclusive argument and a conclusive proof of the truth of what he brought them and the invalidity of what they are doing of worshipping idols that neither benefit nor harm, but are inanimate objects that do not hear or see and do not befriend or be hostile to each other. Only God alone deserves sincere worship, with no partner for Him, in whose hand is the kingdom and to Him belongs the disposition, and there is nothing except under His kingdom, His power and His authority. There is no god but Him and no lord but Him.

11:57: Hud says to them: If you turn away from what I have brought you of worshipping God, your Lord, alone, without partner, then the proof has been established against you by my conveying to you the message of God with which He sent me. And my Lord will replace you with a people other than you, who will worship Him alone, not associating partners with Him, and He does not care about you, for you will not harm Him with your disbelief, but the consequences of that will come back to you. Indeed, my Lord is Guardian over all things, meaning He witnesses and preserves the words and actions of His servants, and He rewards them for them, whether good or evil. And when Our command came, which was the barren wind, God destroyed them all and saved Hud and his followers from a severe punishment by His mercy and kindness. And those were ‘Aad, who denied the signs of their Lord, they disbelieved in them and disobeyed the messengers of God. This is because whoever disbelieves in a prophet has disbelieved in all the prophets, because there is no difference between any of them in the obligation of belief in him. So the ‘Aad disbelieved in Hud, so their disbelief was placed in the same position as someone who disbelieved in all the messengers. “And they followed The command of every stubborn tyrant "They abandoned following their righteous Messenger? And they followed the command of every stubborn tyrant, so for this reason they were followed in this world by a curse from God and from His believing servants whenever they were mentioned and it was called out to them on the Day of Resurrection before all witnesses, "Indeed, the 'Aad people disbelieved in their Lord" the verse. Al-Suddi said: No prophet was sent after 'Aad except that they were cursed on his tongue.

11:61: God Almighty says: And We sent to Thamud who were the ones who inhabited the cities of Hijr between Tabuk and Medina and were after ‘Ad, so God sent from them their brother Salih and he commanded them to worship God alone, and for this reason He said: He created you from the earth meaning He began your creation from it, He created from it your father Adam and settled you in it meaning He made you inhabit it and make use of it so seek forgiveness of Him for your past sins then repent to Him in what you will do for my Lord is near and responsive as God Almighty said: “And when My servants ask you concerning Me - indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me” the verse.
11:62: The Almighty mentions what was said between Salih, peace be upon him, and his people, and what was of ignorance and stubbornness in their saying, You were among us a source of hope before this, meaning we had hope in you in your mind before you said what you said, Do you forbid us from worshipping what our fathers worshipped? and what our ancestors were upon, And indeed, we are in doubt concerning that to which you invite us, disquieting, meaning much doubt. He said, ‘O my people, have you considered? If I am upon clear evidence from my Lord,’ in what He sent me to you with certainty and proof, and He has given me mercy from Himself, then who can help me against God if I disobey Him? and abandon your call to the truth and the worship of God alone? If I had abandoned it, you would not have benefited me and you would not have increased me, except loss, meaning loss.

11:69: God Almighty says: And Our messengers came - they are the angels - to Abraham with good tidings. It was said that they gave him good tidings of Isaac, and it was said that they gave him good tidings of the destruction of the people of Lot. The first is supported by God Almighty's statement: So when the fear had departed from Abraham and the good tidings had come to him, he began to argue with Us concerning the people of Lot. "They said, 'Peace.' He said, 'Peace.'" That is, upon you. The scholars of rhetoric said: This is better than what they greeted him with, because the nominative case indicates permanence and continuity. "And he did not delay in bringing a roasted calf" - that is, he went quickly and brought them hospitality, which was a young cow calf. Haneeth: roasted on embers, which are hot stones. This is the meaning of what was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Qatadah and others, as he said in the other verse: “He went to his family and brought a fattened calf. And he brought it near to them. He said, ‘Will you not eat?’” This verse includes the etiquette of hospitality from many aspects. His statement: But when he saw that their hands did not reach it, he disliked them disliked them and felt fear of them because the angels had no interest in food, nor did they desire it or eat it. For this reason, he saw their condition, turning away from what he had brought to them, completely empty of it. At that point, he disliked them and felt fear of them Al-Suddi said: When God sent the angels to the people of Lot, they came walking in the forms of young men until they descended upon Abraham to host him. When he saw their end, He went to his family and brought a fattened calf so he slaughtered it, then roasted it on the coals and brought it to them. He sat with them and Sarah stood to serve them. This is when he says - and his wife was standing while he was sitting - in the reading of Ibn Mas’ud “and he brought it near to them. He said, ‘Will you not eat?’” They said: O Abraham, we do not eat food. Except for a price. He said: This has a price. They said: What is its price? He said: You mention the name of God at the beginning and praise Him at the end. Gabriel looked at Michael and said: This one deserves that his Lord should take him as a friend. But when he saw that their hands did not reach toward him, he disliked them. When Sarah saw that he had honored them and she stood up to serve them, she laughed and said: How strange are these guests of ours! We serve them ourselves out of honor for them, and they do not eat our food. Ibn Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Nasr bin Ali told us, Noah bin Qais told us, on the authority of Othman bin Mohsen, regarding the guests of Abraham, he said: They were four: Gabriel, Michael, Israfil, and Raphael. Noah bin Qais said: Noah bin Abi Shaddad claimed that when they entered upon Abraham and he brought the calf to them, Gabriel stroked it with his wing, so it stood up and ran until it joined its mother and the mother of the calf in the house. And the Almighty’s statement, informing about the angels: They said, ‘Do not fear,’ means they said, Do not fear us, we are angels sent to the people of Lot to destroy them. Then he walked a little and repeated that to them until he repeated it four times. Qatada said that they had been ordered not to destroy them until their prophet testified against them about that. She said, Stay where you are until I come to you. So some of her people separated from them and she came to her father and said, “O my father, find some young men at the gate of the city. Rather, you are a transgressing people. And his statement in another verse, “They said, ‘Have you not come to the males of the worlds? And forsake what your Lord has created for you as mates. Rather, you are a transgressing people.’” We forbid you from the worlds” meaning, did we not forbid you from hosting men? “He said, ‘These are my daughters, if you are to do something. By your life, they are in their intoxication, wandering blindly.’” And he said about this noble verse: These are my daughters; they are purer for you. And indeed you know what we want. meaning we have no desire except for males, and you know that, so what is the need to repeat this statement to us? As-Suddi said: And indeed you know what we want. We only want men.

11:80: God Almighty says, informing about His Prophet Lot, peace be upon him, that Lot threatened them by saying: If I had power over you the verse, meaning I would have punished you and done to you the deeds of myself and my clan, and for this reason it was mentioned in the hadith on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr bin Alqamah bin Abi Salamah on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God's mercy be upon Lot, he used to seek refuge in a strong support - meaning God Almighty - and God did not send after him a prophet except in the wealth of his people. Then the angels informed him that they were God's messengers to them and that they would not be able to reach him. They said, O Lot, indeed we are messengers of your Lord; they will never reach you. And they ordered him to set out with his family at the end of the night and to follow their backs, meaning to be a rear guard for his family. And let none of you turn back, meaning if you hear what has happened to them, do not be frightened by those disturbing sounds, but continue going. Except your wife. Most said that it is an exception from The confirmed one is his saying: So set out with your family, meaning except your wife, and Ibn Masoud read it in this way. These people put your wife in the accusative case because it is from the confirmed one, so it was obligatory for them to put it in the accusative case. Others from the reciters and grammarians said that it is an exception to his saying: And let none of you look back except your wife, so they permitted the nominative and the accusative cases. They mentioned that she went out with them and that when she heard the meal she turned around and said: Oh my people! Then a stone came from the sky and killed her. Then they brought him close to the destruction of his people as good report for him because he said to them, Destroy them now! They said, “Indeed, their appointed time is the morning. Is not the morning near?” This was while the people of Lot were standing at the door, swarming toward him from every side, and Lot was standing at the door, defending them, deterring them, and forbidding them from what they were doing, but they did not accept him, rather they threatened him and intimidated him. Then Gabriel, peace be upon him, came out to them and struck their faces with his wing, blinding their eyes, so they returned without finding their way, as God Almighty said: “And they certainly tried to seduce him from his guest, but We blinded their eyes. So taste My punishment and warning.” The verse. Muammar said on the authority of Qatadah on the authority of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, who said: Abraham, peace be upon him, used to come to the people of Lot and say, God has forbidden you from exposing yourself to His punishment, but they did not obey him until the time for the book reached its end. The angels came to Lot while he was working in his land, so he called them. To hospitality, they said, We are your guests tonight. God had promised Gabriel that He would not punish them until Lot testified against them three times. When Lot took them to hospitality, he mentioned the evil his people were doing. He walked with them for a while, then turned to them and said, "Do you not know what the people of this village are doing? I do not know of anyone on the face of the earth who is worse than them. Where shall I take you? To my people, who are the worst of God's creation." Gabriel turned to the angels and said, Guard this one. Then he walked with them for a while. When he reached the middle of the village, he felt compassion for them and felt shy of them, and said, "Do you not know what the people of this village are doing? I do not know of anyone on the face of the earth who is worse than them. My people are the worst of God's creation." Gabriel turned to the angels and said, Guard these two. When he reached the door of the house, he cried out of shame and compassion for them, and said, "My people are the worst of God's creation. Do you not know what the people of this village are doing? I do not know of anyone on the face of the earth who is worse than them." Gabriel said to the angels: Remember these three things, for the punishment has come. So when they entered, the evil old woman went up and waved her garment, and the wicked ones came running to her and said: What do you have? Lot's guests said: There are people whom I have never seen more beautiful faces or more pleasant smelling than them. They rushed to the door, and Lot confronted them at the door, but they pushed him away for a long time, while he was inside and they were outside, imploring God and saying: These are my daughters, they are purer for you. Then the angel Falaz stood at the door - he said: He pulled it up - and asked Gabriel's permission to punish them, so God gave him permission. He stood in the form in which he is in heaven, and spread his wing - Gabriel has two wings - and he was wearing a scarf of strung pearls, and his front teeth were shining, his forehead was broad, and his head was like coral, which is pearls, as if it were snow, and his feet were green. He said: O Lot, we are messengers of your Lord; they will never reach you. Go, O Lot, from the door and leave me and them. So Lot stepped aside from the door and went out to them, and spread his wing and struck their faces with it, blinding their eyes, so they became blind and could not know the way. Then he ordered Lot to be carried with his family that night. He said: So travel with your family during a part of the night. It was narrated: On the authority of Muhammad bin Kaab, Qatada and Al-Suddi, something similar to this.

11:82: God Almighty says: So when Our command came and that was at sunrise We made its upper part which is Sodom its lower part as He says: And that which covered it covered it meaning We rained down upon it stones of baked clay which in Persian means stones of clay, as Ibn Abbas and others said. Some of them said that is from sink which is stone and kul which is clay. He said in the other verse stones of clay meaning hard, strong, and some of them said roasted. Al-Bukhari said that sajil means the strong, the great. Sajil and Sijjin, the lam and the nun are sisters. Tamim bin Muqbil said: A man beats the eggs, the owner of the beating, the heroes communicated with him, a prisoner And his saying: arranged Some of them said: in the sky, meaning prepared for that. And others said: arranged meaning one follows the other in its descent upon them. And his saying: marked meaning marked and sealed with the names of its owners, each stone is written with the name of the one upon whom it descends. And Qatada and Ikrimah said: marked surrounded by a reddish glow. And they mentioned that it was revealed upon the people of the city and upon those scattered in the villages around it. So while one of them was talking with the people, a stone came to him from the sky and fell upon him from among the people and destroyed him. So the stones followed them from all the countries until they destroyed them to the last one, and not one of them remained. And Mujahid said: Gabriel took the people of Lot from their pastures and homes, carried them with their livestock and their belongings, and lifted them up until the people of the sky heard the barking of their dogs, then he tipped them over, and he carried them on the edges of his right wing. He said: And when he turned it over, the first thing to fall from it were its balconies. And Qatada said: It has reached us that Gabriel took hold of the middle handle of the city, then he turned it into the atmosphere of the sky until the people of the sky heard the roaring of the people. Their dogs then destroyed some of them on top of each other then the scum of the people followed Sakhr he said and it was mentioned to us that they were four villages in each village a hundred thousand and in another narration three villages the largest of them is Sodom, he said and it reached us that Abraham, peace be upon him, was looking out over Sodom and saying: Sodom is a day of destruction and in a narration from Qatada and others he said and it reached us that when Gabriel, peace be upon him, woke up he spread his wing and blew up their land with it including its palaces and animals and stones and trees and everything in it and he gathered it in his wing and folded it and folded it in the hollow of his wing then he ascended with it to the lowest heaven until the inhabitants of the heaven heard the voices of people and dogs and they were four thousand then he turned it upside down and sent it to the earth upside down and he crushed some of it on top of others so he made its top its bottom then he followed it with stones of baked clay, and Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi said: The villages of the people of Lot were five villages Sodom and they are the greatest and difficult and ascending and ascending and ascending with it until the inhabitants of the lowest heaven heard the barking of its dogs And the sounds of her chickens, then he threw her on her face, then God followed her with stones. God the Most High says: And We turned it upside down and rained upon it stones of baked clay. So God destroyed it and the surrounding lands of the overturned ones. Al-Suddi said: When the people of Lot woke up, Gabriel came down and uprooted the earth from seven lands and carried it until he reached the sky until the people of the lowest heaven heard the barking of their dogs and the sounds of their roosters, then he turned it over and killed them. That is what He said: And the overturned ones are inclined. And whoever did not die until he fell to the ground, God rained stones upon him while he was under the ground. And whoever among them was an outcast in the land following them in the villages, so a man would talk and a stone would come to him and kill him. That is what God the Almighty said: And We rained upon them meaning in the villages stones of baked clay. This is what Al-Suddi said. And His statement: And it is not far from the wrongdoers means this punishment is not far from those who resemble them in their wrongdoing. It was mentioned in the hadith narrated in the Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, Whoever you find doing the work of the people of Lot, kill the doer. And the one to whom it is done. Imam Al-Shafi’i, in a statement from him and a group of scholars, said that the sodomite should be killed, whether he is married or not, based on this hadith. Imam Abu Hanifa said that he should be thrown from a high place and followed with stones, as God did with the people of Lot. God Almighty knows best.
11:83: God Almighty says: So when Our command came and that was at sunrise We made its upper part which is Sodom its lower part as He says: And that which covered it covered it meaning We rained down upon it stones of baked clay which in Persian means stones of clay, as Ibn Abbas and others said. Some of them said that is from sink which is stone and kul which is clay. He said in the other verse stones of clay meaning hard, strong, and some of them said roasted. Al-Bukhari said that sajil means the strong, the great. Sajil and Sijjin, the lam and the nun are sisters. Tamim bin Muqbil said: A man beats the eggs, the owner of the beating, the heroes communicated with him, a prisoner And his saying: arranged Some of them said: in the sky, meaning prepared for that. And others said: arranged meaning one follows the other in its descent upon them. And his saying: marked meaning marked and sealed with the names of its owners, each stone is written with the name of the one upon whom it descends. And Qatada and Ikrimah said: marked surrounded by a reddish glow. And they mentioned that it was revealed upon the people of the city and upon those scattered in the villages around it. So while one of them was talking with the people, a stone came to him from the sky and fell upon him from among the people and destroyed him. So the stones followed them from all the countries until they destroyed them to the last one, and not one of them remained. And Mujahid said: Gabriel took the people of Lot from their pastures and homes, carried them with their livestock and their belongings, and lifted them up until the people of the sky heard the barking of their dogs, then he tipped them over, and he carried them on the edges of his right wing. He said: And when he turned it over, the first thing to fall from it were its balconies. And Qatada said: It has reached us that Gabriel took hold of the middle handle of the city, then he turned it into the atmosphere of the sky until the people of the sky heard the roaring of the people. Their dogs then destroyed some of them on top of each other then the scum of the people followed Sakhr he said and it was mentioned to us that they were four villages in each village a hundred thousand and in another narration three villages the largest of them is Sodom, he said and it reached us that Abraham, peace be upon him, was looking out over Sodom and saying: Sodom is a day of destruction and in a narration from Qatada and others he said and it reached us that when Gabriel, peace be upon him, woke up he spread his wing and blew up their land with it including its palaces and animals and stones and trees and everything in it and he gathered it in his wing and folded it and folded it in the hollow of his wing then he ascended with it to the lowest heaven until the inhabitants of the heaven heard the voices of people and dogs and they were four thousand then he turned it upside down and sent it to the earth upside down and he crushed some of it on top of others so he made its top its bottom then he followed it with stones of baked clay, and Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi said: The villages of the people of Lot were five villages Sodom and they are the greatest and difficult and ascending and ascending and ascending with it until the inhabitants of the lowest heaven heard the barking of its dogs And the sounds of her chickens, then he threw her on her face, then God followed her with stones. God the Most High says: And We turned it upside down and rained upon it stones of baked clay. So God destroyed it and the surrounding lands of the overturned ones. Al-Suddi said: When the people of Lot woke up, Gabriel came down and uprooted the earth from seven lands and carried it until he reached the sky until the people of the lowest heaven heard the barking of their dogs and the sounds of their roosters, then he turned it over and killed them. That is what He said: And the overturned ones are inclined. And whoever did not die until he fell to the ground, God rained stones upon him while he was under the ground. And whoever among them was an outcast in the land following them in the villages, so a man would talk and a stone would come to him and kill him. That is what God the Almighty said: And We rained upon them meaning in the villages stones of baked clay. This is what Al-Suddi said. And His statement: And it is not far from the wrongdoers means this punishment is not far from those who resemble them in their wrongdoing. It was mentioned in the hadith narrated in the Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, Whoever you find doing the work of the people of Lot, kill the doer. Imam Abu Hanifa said that he should be thrown from a high place and followed with stones, as God did with the people of Lot. God Almighty knows best.
11:84: God the Almighty says: And We had certainly sent to Madyan, a tribe of Arabs who lived between the Hijaz and the Levant, near Ma'an. A land known to them was called Madyan. So God sent to them Shu'ayb, who was one of the most noble of them in lineage. That is why He said: Their brother Shu'ayb, ordering them to worship God the Almighty alone, with no partner, and forbidding them from cheating in the measure and weight. Indeed, I see you well, meaning in your livelihood and provision, and I fear that you will be robbed of what you are in by violating God's prohibitions. And indeed, I fear for you the punishment of an encompassing Day, meaning in the Hereafter.
11:85: He first forbade them from reducing the measure and weight if they gave to people, then he ordered them to fulfill the measure and weight fairly, taking and giving, and he forbade them from spreading corruption on the earth, as they used to cut off the road, and his saying: What remains from God is better for you Ibn Abbas said: God's provision is better for you, and Al-Hasan said: God's provision is better for you than people defrauding you, and Al-Rabi' bin Anas said: God's commandment is better for you, and Mujahid said: Obedience to God, and Qatada said: Your portion from God is better for you, and Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: Destruction is in the punishment and what remains is in mercy, and Abu Ja'far bin Jarir said: What remains from God is better for you meaning what remains for you of profit after fulfilling the measure and weight is better for you than taking people's money, he said: This has been narrated from Ibn Abbas, I said: It is similar to the saying of God the Almighty: "Say: The bad and the good are not equal, even though the abundance of the bad pleases you" and the verse, and his saying: And I am not a guardian over you meaning a watcher nor a guardian, meaning do that For God Almighty, do not do it for people to see you, but for God Almighty.

11:87: They say to him in mockery, may God curse them, Your prayer Al-A'mash said, meaning your recitation, Order you to leave what our fathers worshipped meaning the idols and statues, or to do with our wealth as we wish so you leave the fraudulent statement, which is our wealth, we do with it as we wish. Al-Hasan said in his statement, Your prayer orders you to leave what our fathers worshipped meaning, by God, his prayer orders them to leave what their fathers worshipped. Al-Thawri said in his statement, Or to do with our wealth as we wish meaning zakat, Indeed, you are the forbearing, the rightly guided. Ibn Abbas, Maymun ibn Mihran, Ibn Jurayj, Ibn Aslam, and Ibn Jarir said that the enemies of God say that in mockery, may God curse them and curse them for their mercy, and they have done so.
11:88: He says to them, have you seen, O people, if I am on clear evidence from my Lord meaning, on insight into what I call to, and He has provided me from Him a good provision It was said that he meant prophethood, and it was said that he meant lawful provision, and it is possible for both matters. Al-Thawri said, And I do not intend to go against you in what I forbid you from meaning, I do not forbid you from something and I go against it in secret, so I do it hidden from you, as Qatada said in his statement, And I do not intend to go against you in what I forbid you from He said: I did not forbid you from a matter and then commit it. I only desire reform as much as I am able meaning, in what I command you and forbid you. I only desire your reform as much as I can and as much as I can. And my success meaning, in hitting the truth in what I want, "is only in God. In Him I have relied" in all my affairs, and to Him I turn meaning, I return. Mujahid and others said this. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, Abu Qaz'ah Suwaid bin Hujayr al-Bahili told us, on the authority of Hakim bin Mu'awiyah, on the authority of his father, that his brother Malik said: O Muawiyah, Muhammad has taken my neighbors, so go to him, for he has spoken to you and knows you. So I went with him, and he said: Leave my neighbors for me, for they had become Muslims. So he turned away from him, and he stood up angrily and said: By God, if you do that, the people will claim that you order us to do something and then go against it, and you will be paid while he is speaking. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you say? He said: By God, if you do that, the people will claim that you order us to do something and then go against it. He said: He said: Or have they said it - meaning their speaker - and if I do that, then it is only against me and they have nothing to do with it. Send his neighbors to him. He also said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Bahz ibn Hakim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took some people from my people on suspicion and detained them. Then a man from my people came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was delivering a sermon and said: O Muhammad, why are you detaining my neighbors? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was silent, then he said: Some people say that you forbid something and then you leave it alone. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: What do you say? I began to exchange words between them for fear that he might hear it and invoke a curse upon my people from which they would never prosper. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) kept on talking until he understood it, then he said: They said it, or someone among them said it. By God, if I did, it would be upon me and what was upon them. They would leave their neighbors alone. And of this type is the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad. Abu Amir told us, Sulayman ibn Bilal told us, on the authority of Rabi’ah ibn Abi Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Abd al-Malik ibn Sa’id ibn Suwayd al-Ansari, who said: I heard Abu Hamid and Abu Asid saying that he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: If you hear a hadith from me and your hearts recognize it, and your hair and skin soften to it, and you think that it is close to you, then I am the most deserving of it. But if you hear a hadith from me and your hearts reject it, and your hair and skin are repelled by it, and you think that it is far from you, then I am the furthest from it. Its chain of transmission is sound. Muslim narrated with this chain of transmission the hadith: “When one of you enters the mosque, let him say: O God, open for me the doors of Your mercy, and when he leaves, let him say: O God, I ask You for Your bounty.” Its meaning is: And God knows best. Whatever good you hear about me, I am the first to receive it. And whatever bad thing I am, I am the furthest from it. And I do not wish to go against you in that which I forbid you from. Qatadah said on the authority of Azra on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Arni on the authority of Yahya bin Al-Jazzar on the authority of Masruq, who said: A woman came to Ibn Mas’ud and said: Do you forbid extensions? He said: Yes. She said: One of your wives did it. He said: You have not memorized the advice of the righteous slave, then. And I do not wish to go against you in that which I forbid you from. Uthman bin Abi Shaybah said: Jarir narrated to us on the authority of Abu Sulayman Al-Utbi, who said: Letters of Umar bin Abdul Aziz would come to us in which there were commands and prohibitions, and he would write at the end of them, and I did not do anything except as the righteous slave said: “And my success is only through God. Upon Him I rely and to Him I turn.”
11:89: He says to them, "O my people, do not let my dissent lead you to persist in your disbelief and corruption, lest you be afflicted with the same punishment and torment that befell the people of Noah, the people of Hud, the people of Salih, and the people of Lot. Qatada said, O my people, do not let my dissent lead you to persist in your misguidance and disbelief, lest you be afflicted with the same torment that befell them. Al-Suddi said, My enmity lead you to persist in your misguidance and disbelief, lest you be afflicted with the same torment that befell them. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad Ibn Auf Al-Himsi told us, Abu Al-Mughira Abdul Quddus Ibn Al-Hajjaj told us, Ibn Abi Ghania told us, Abdul Malik Ibn Abi Sulayman told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila Al-Kindi, who said: I was with my master, holding his mount, and the people had surrounded Uthman Ibn Affan, when he looked out at us from his house and said: O my people, do not let my dissension prevent you from suffering what happened to the people of Noah, or the people of Hud, or the people of Salih. O my people, do not kill me, for if you kill me, you will be like this, and he interlaced his fingers. His statement: And the people of Lot are not far from you, it was said that what is meant is in time. Qatada said: He means that they perished before you yesterday. It was said that it is in place, and both meanings are possible. And seek forgiveness of your Lord for past sins, and then repent to Him for the evil deeds that you will do in the future. His statement: Indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Loving to those who repent.

11:91: They say, "O Shu'aib, we do not understand we do not understand much of what you say and indeed we see you weak among us Sa'id bin Jubayr and Ath-Thawri said, and he was blind, and Ath-Thawri said that he was called the orator of the prophets, Al-Suddi said, and indeed we see you weak among us" he said: You are one, and Abu Rawq said: They mean humiliated because your clan is not of your religion "and if it were not for your people, we would have stoned you" meaning your people, if it were not for their esteem over us, we would have stoned you. It was said with stones and it was said that we cursed you "and you are not mighty over us meaning we do not have esteem for you He said, O my people, is my family more mighty over you than God" he said: Do you leave me for the sake of my people and do not leave me out of respect for the Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, that you may harm His Prophet while you have taken the Book of God "behind you on your back meaning you have thrown it behind you, neither obeying it nor honoring it indeed, my Lord encompasses what you do meaning He knows everything Your deeds and He will reward you for them.

It was said with stones and it was said that we cursed you and you are not mighty over us meaning we do not have esteem for you He said, O my people, is my family more mighty over you than God he said: Do you leave me for the sake of my people and do not leave me out of respect for the Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, that you may harm His Prophet while you have taken the Book of God behind you on your back meaning you have thrown it behind you, neither obeying it nor honoring it indeed, my Lord encompasses what you do meaning He knows everything Your deeds and He will reward you for them.
11:93: When the Prophet of God, Shu'aib, despaired of their response to him, he said, O my people, act according to your position, meaning your way, and this is a severe threat. I am acting, according to my way. You will soon know who will be afflicted with a punishment that will disgrace him and who is a liar, meaning from me and from you. And watch, meaning wait, I am with you, watching. God Almighty said, "And when Our command came, We saved Shu'aib and those who believed with him by mercy from Us. And the blast seized those who did wrong, and they became within their homes fallen down." His saying fallen down means lifeless, with no movement in them. And here He mentioned that a shout came to them, and in Al-A’raf, a tremor, and in Ash-Shu’ara, the punishment of the Day of the Shadow, and they are one nation, and all these punishments were gathered upon them on the Day of their punishment. Rather, He mentioned in each context what was appropriate for it. In Al-A’raf, when they said, We will surely expel you, O Shu’aib, and those who believed with you from our city, it was appropriate to mention the tremor, the tremor, so the land in which they had wronged shook with them and they wanted to expel their Prophet from it. And here, when they were ill-mannered in their speech to their Prophet, He mentioned the shout that delayed them and extinguished them. And in Ash-Shu’ara, when they said, Then let down upon us fragments from the sky, if you should be of the truthful, He said, “So the punishment of the Day of the Shadow seized them. Indeed, it was the punishment of a tremendous Day.” This is one of the subtle secrets, and praise and thanks are due to God abundantly and always. And His saying, As if they had never prospered therein, meaning they had never lived in their home before that, Away with Midian, as Thamud was away, and they were their neighbors, close to them in the home and similar to them in disbelief and highway robbery, and they were Arabs like them.

11:96: God Almighty says, informing us about sending Moses with his signs and dazzling evidence to Pharaoh, the king of the Copts, and his al-Nas 114:So they followed the command of Pharaoh, meaning his method, conduct, and way of error. And Pharaoh’s command was not right, meaning there was no right guidance or direction in it. Rather, it is ignorance, misguidance, disbelief and stubbornness. Just as they followed him in this world and he was their leader and chief, so he will lead them on the Day of Resurrection to the fire of Hell, so he will lead them into it and they will drink from its filthy pools. He will have the greatest share of the greatest punishment, as God the Almighty said: But Pharaoh disobeyed the Messenger, so We seized him with a terrible punishment. And God the Almighty said: “But he denied and disobeyed. Then he turned back, striving. So he was gathered together and cried out. And he said, ‘I am your Lord, the Most High.’ So God seized him with the punishment of the Hereafter and the first. Indeed in that is a lesson for whoever fears.” And God the Almighty said: He will lead his people on the Day of Resurrection and will lead them into the Fire, and wretched is the destination. And likewise the way of those who are followed, they will be abundant in the punishment on the Day of Resurrection, as God the Almighty said: For each is double, but you do not know. And God the Almighty said, informing about the disbelievers that they will say in the Fire: “Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters and our dignitaries, and they led us astray from the way. Our Lord, give them double the punishment.” And Imam Ahmad said: Hisham told us, Abu al-Jahm told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri narrated on the authority of Abu Salamah on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Imru’ al-Qais is the standard-bearer of the poets of the Age of Ignorance to the Fire. His statement: And they were pursued in this world by a curse and on the Day of Resurrection, the verse, means that We pursued them in addition to the punishment of the Fire by a curse in this world and on the Day of Resurrection. What an evil provision is that? Mujahid said: They were pursued by the curse on the Day of Resurrection, so those are two curses. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: What an evil provision is that? He said: The curse of this world and the Hereafter. Ad-Dahhak and Qatadah said the same, and it is like His statement: “And We made them leaders inviting to the Fire, but on the Day of Resurrection they will not be aided. And We pursued them in this world by a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the despised.” And God, the Most High, said: “The Fire, they will be exposed to it morning and evening. And on the Day the Hour will appear, ‘Admit the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment.’”

And on the Day the Hour will appear, ‘Admit the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment.’”
11:98: God Almighty says, informing us about sending Moses with his signs and dazzling evidence to Pharaoh, the king of the Copts, and his al-Nas 114:So they followed the command of Pharaoh, meaning his method, conduct, and way of error. And Pharaoh’s command was not right, meaning there was no right guidance or direction in it. Rather, it is ignorance, misguidance, disbelief and stubbornness. Just as they followed him in this world and he was their leader and chief, so he will lead them on the Day of Resurrection to the fire of Hell, so he will lead them into it and they will drink from its filthy pools. He will have the greatest share of the greatest punishment, as God the Almighty said: But Pharaoh disobeyed the Messenger, so We seized him with a terrible punishment. And God the Almighty said: “But he denied and disobeyed. Then he turned back, striving. So he was gathered together and cried out. And he said, ‘I am your Lord, the Most High.’ So God seized him with the punishment of the Hereafter and the first. Indeed in that is a lesson for whoever fears.” And God the Almighty said: He will lead his people on the Day of Resurrection and will lead them into the Fire, and wretched is the destination. And likewise the way of those who are followed, they will be abundant in the punishment on the Day of Resurrection, as God the Almighty said: For each is double, but you do not know. And God the Almighty said, informing about the disbelievers that they will say in the Fire: “Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters and our dignitaries, and they led us astray from the way. Our Lord, give them double the punishment.” And Imam Ahmad said: Hisham told us, Abu al-Jahm told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri narrated on the authority of Abu Salamah on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Imru’ al-Qais is the standard-bearer of the poets of the Age of Ignorance to the Fire.
