11:100: When God Almighty mentioned the report of the prophets and what happened to them with their nations and how He destroyed the disbelievers and saved the believers, He said: This is from the report of the towns, meaning their report, We relate to you some of them standing, meaning populated, and some harvested, meaning destroyed. And We did not wrong them, meaning when We destroyed them, but they wronged themselves, by denying Our messengers and disbelieving in them. So their gods, their idols that they worshipped and called upon, besides God, did not avail them at all, they did not benefit them nor did they save them when God’s command to destroy them came. And they only increased them in destruction. Mujahid, Qatadah, and others said: “That is, other than loss. This is because the reason for their destruction and ruin was only their following those gods, and for this reason they lost in this world and the hereafter.
11:101: When God Almighty mentioned the report of the prophets and what happened to them with their nations and how He destroyed the disbelievers and saved the believers, He said: This is from the report of the towns, meaning their report, We relate to you some of them standing, meaning populated, and some harvested, meaning destroyed. And We did not wrong them, meaning when We destroyed them, but they wronged themselves, by denying Our messengers and disbelieving in them. So their gods, their idols that they worshipped and called upon, besides God, did not avail them at all, they did not benefit them nor did they save them when God’s command to destroy them came. And they only increased them in destruction. Mujahid, Qatadah, and others said: “That is, other than loss. This is because the reason for their destruction and ruin was only their following those gods, and for this reason they lost in this world and the hereafter.
11:102: God Almighty says: Just as We destroyed those unjust generations who denied Our messengers, so will We deal with those like them. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Musa, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed, God gives respite to the wrongdoer until, when He seizes him, He does not let him escape. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: And such is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are doing wrong. The verse.
11:103: God Almighty says that in our destruction of the unbelievers and our salvation of the believers there is a sign that is, a lesson and a consideration of the truth of our promise in the afterlife. Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe during the worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses will stand. God Almighty also says, Then their Lord inspired to them, ‘We will surely destroy the wrongdoers.’ And His statement: That is a Day when mankind will be gathered together meaning the first and the last of them, like His statement: And We will gather them together and will not leave out a single one of them “And that is a witnessed Day” meaning a great Day in which the angels will attend and the messengers will gather and all of creation will be gathered from mankind, jinn, birds, beasts and animals, and the Just One will judge in it who will not wrong an atom’s weight, and if there is a good deed, He will multiply it. And His statement: And We do not delay it except for a specified term meaning We do not delay the establishment of the Resurrection except because the word of God preceded in the existence of a specified number of people from the descendants of Adam and He set a specific period, if it ends and the existence of those destined to emerge is complete, the Hour will come. For this reason He said: And We do not delay it except for a specified term meaning for a limited period that will not be increased or decreased. On the Day it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission meaning on the Day when the Day of Resurrection comes, no one will speak except by God’s permission, like His statement: They will not speak except he whom the Most Merciful permits and who says what is right and He said: And the voices will be hushed before the Most Merciful the verse. In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of intercession: “On that Day none will speak except the Messengers, and the call of the Messengers on that Day will be: ‘O God, save, save.’” And His statement: Among them are the wretched and the blessed, meaning that among the people of the gathering are the wretched and among them are the blessed, as He said: A group in Paradise and a group in the Blaze. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said in his Musnad: Musa ibn Hayyan told us, Abdul-Malik ibn Amr told us, Sulayman Abu Sufyan told us, Abdullah ibn Dinar told us, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of Umar, who said: When Among them are the wretched and the blessed, was revealed, I asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I said: O Messenger of God, what should we act upon? On something that has already been completed or on something that has not yet been completed? He said: On something that has already been completed, O Umar, and the pens have written about it, but each is facilitated for what he was created for. Then God, the Most High, explained the state of the wretched and the state of the blessed, saying: God swears by the heaven and its constellations, which are the great stars, as was previously explained in His statement: Blessed is He who has placed in the heaven constellations and placed therein a lamp and a moon giving light. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and As-Suddi said: The constellations are the stars. Mujahid also said: The constellations in which are the guards. Yahya ibn Rafi’ said: The constellations are palaces in the heaven. Al-Minhal ibn Amr said: And the heaven with the constellations means beautiful creation. Ibn Jarir preferred that they are the mansions of the sun and the moon, which are twelve constellations. The sun travels through each of them for a month and the moon travels through each of them for two and a third days, so that is twenty-eight mansions and it lasts for two nights. And the Almighty said: And the Promised Day * And a witness and witnessed. The commentators differed on that. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Amr al-Ghazi told us, Ubaydullah - meaning Ibn Musa - told us, Musa bin Ubaidah told us, on the authority of Ayoub bin Khalid bin Safwan bin Aws al-Ansari, on the authority of Abdullah bin Rafi’, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And the Promised Day is the Day of Resurrection. And a witness is Friday. The sun does not rise or set on a day better than Friday. In it is an hour in which no Muslim servant asks God for good except that He gives it to him, and he does not seek refuge in Him from evil except that He protects him. And witnessed is the Day of Arafah. Ibn Khuzaymah narrated this hadith in this way through various chains of transmission on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah al-Rabdhi, whose hadith is weak. It was narrated as being attributed to Abu Hurayrah, which is more likely. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad told us, Shu’bah told us, I heard Ali bin Zaid and Yunus bin Ubaid narrating on the authority of Ammar, the freed slave of Banu Hashim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah. As for Ali, he traced it back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. As for Yunus, he did not mention Abu Hurairah that he said about this verse, And a witness and what is witnessed. He said, He means the witness on Friday, and the witnessed day is the Day of Resurrection. Ahmad also said: Muhammad bin Ja’far told us, Shu’bah told us on the authority of Yunus, I heard Ammar, the freed slave of Banu Hashim narrating on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he said about this verse, And a witness and what is witnessed. He said, The witness is on Friday, and what is witnessed is the Day of Arafah, and what is promised is the Day of Resurrection. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he said: The promised day is the Day of Resurrection. Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said the same, and I have not seen them differ on that, praise be to God. Then Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Awf told us, Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Ayyash told us, my father told us, Damdam ibn Zur’ah told us, on the authority of Shureih ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Abu Malik al-Ash’ari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The promised day is the Day of Resurrection, and the witness is Friday, and the witnessed is the Day of Arafah, and God has saved Friday for us. Then Ibn Jarir said: Sahl bin Musa al-Razi told us, Ibn Abi Fadik told us, on the authority of Ibn Harmalah, on the authority of Saeed bin al-Musayyab, that he said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: The master of days is Friday, and it is the witness and the witnessed, the Day of Arafah. This is a mursal from the mursals of Saeed bin al-Musayyab. Then Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Yusuf al-Makki, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The witness is Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. Then he recited: That is the Day when mankind will be gathered together, and that is the Day witnessed. Ibn Humayd told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Shubak, who said: A man asked al-Hasan bin Ali about the witness and the witnessed. He said: Did you ask anyone before me? He said: Yes, I asked Ibn Omar and Ibn Al-Zubayr and they said: The day of sacrifice and Friday. He said: No, but the witness is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he recited: How will it be then, when We bring from every nation a witness and We bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness over these? And the witness is the Day of Resurrection. Then he recited: That is a Day when the people will be gathered together, and that is a witnessed Day. And this is what Al-Hasan Al-Basri said, and Sufyan Al-Thawri said on the authority of Ibn Harmalah on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab: And the one witnessed on the Day of Resurrection. Mujahid, Ikrimah and Al-Dahhak said: The witness is the son of Adam, and the one witnessed on the Day of Resurrection. And also on the authority of Ikrimah: The witness is Muhammad, peace be upon him, and the one witnessed is Friday. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The witness is God, and the one witnessed is on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Nu’aim Al-Fadl bin Dukayn told us, Sufyan told us on the authority of Abu Yahya Al-Qattat on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And the witness and the one witnessed. He said: The witness is man, and the one witnessed is on Friday. This is how Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and a witness and what is witnessed: the witness is the Day of Arafah and what is witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. And it was narrated by Sufyan al-Thawri, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: The Day of Sacrifice and the Day of Arafah means the witness and what is witnessed. Ibn Jarir said: And others said: The witnessed is Friday. And they narrated in that regard what Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman told us: My uncle Abdullah ibn Wahb told me, Amr ibn al-Harith told me, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abi Hilal, on the authority of Zaid ibn Ayman, on the authority of Ubadah ibn Nassi, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Increase your prayers for me on Friday, for it is a witnessed day in which the angels witness. And on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr: The witness is God, and he recited: And sufficient is God as a witness, and what is witnessed is us. Al-Baghawi narrated it. And the majority said that the witness is Friday and what is witnessed is the Day of Arafah. God the Almighty said: He cursed the companions of the ditch meaning He cursed the companions of the ditch, the plural of which is akhādīd, which is holes in the ground. This is report about a group of disbelievers who went to those who believed in God the Almighty and subdued them, wanting them to renounce their religion, but they refused. So they dug a ditch in the ground and lit a fire in it, preparing fuel to fuel it. Then they wanted to retaliate but they refused, so they threw them into it. For this reason God the Almighty said: He cursed the companions of the ditch * The fire fueled * When they were sitting by it * And they were witnesses to what they were doing to the believers. God the Almighty said: And they did not find fault with them for anything except that they believed in God, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy. Meaning, they had no sin against them except their belief in God, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy, who does not wrong those who seek refuge in His impregnable side, in all of His words, deeds, laws, and decrees. Even if He had decreed for these servants what befell them at the hands of the disbelievers, then He is the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy, even if the reason for that is hidden from many people. Then God the Almighty said: To whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. The completion of the description is that He is the Owner of all the heavens and the earth and everything in them and between them. And God is Witness over all things. That is, nothing in the heavens or the earth is hidden from Him, and nothing is hidden from Him. The people of interpretation differed about who the people of this story were. According to Ali, they were the people of Persia when their king wanted to permit incest, but their scholars refused them, so he dug a trench and threw into it those who objected to him, and the practice of permitting incest has continued among them to this day. It was narrated from him that they were a people in Yemen whose believers and polytheists fought, and the believers defeated the disbelievers, then they fought and the disbelievers defeated the believers, so they dug trenches for them and burned them in them. It was narrated from him that they were from the people of Abyssinia, and one of them was an Abyssinian. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, The companions of the trench were killed, the fire with fuel. He said: People from the Children of Israel dug a trench in the ground, then they lit a fire in it, then they placed men and women by that trench and paraded them over it, and they claimed that it was Daniel and his companions. This is what Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim said, and other things were said. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Laila, on the authority of Suhaib, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Among those who came before you, there was a king who had a magician. When the magician grew old, he said to the king, ‘I have grown old and my time has come, so give me a boy so that I may teach him magic.’ So he gave him a boy, and he taught him magic. There was a monk between the magic and the king, so the boy went to the monk and listened to his speech, and he liked his manner and speech. When he went to the magician, he would hit him and say, ‘What held you back?’ And when he went to his family, they would hit him and say, ‘What held you back?’ So he complained about that to the monk, and he said, ‘If the magician wants to hit you, say, ‘My family held me back.’ And if your family wants to hit you, say, ‘The magician held me back.’ One day, while he was there, he came upon a huge, terrifying beast that had held people back so that they could not cross. So he said, ‘Today I know whether the matter of the monk is more beloved to God than the matter of magic.’ So he took a stone and said, ‘O God, if the matter of the monk is more beloved to You and more pleasing to You than the matter of the magician, then kill this beast.’” Until the people passed, and he threw it and killed it and the people went and the monk was told about that and he said, My son, you are better than me and you will be tested, so if you are tested do not point me out. So the boy cured the blind and the leper and all other diseases and healed them. The king had a companion who went blind and heard about him so he came to him with many gifts and said, Heal me and you will have what is here collected. He said, “I do not heal anyone, only God Almighty heals. If you believe in Him, I will call upon God and He will heal you.” So he believed and called upon God and He healed him. Then the king came and sat down in the same position as he had been sitting before. The king said to him, O so-and-so, who restored your sight? He said, My Lord. He said, No, my Lord and your Lord is God. He said, Do you have a lord other than me? He said, Yes, my Lord and your Lord is God. He continued torturing him until he directed him to the boy. Then the king sent for him and said, O my son, has your magic reached such an extent that you heal the blind, the leper, and these diseases? He said, I do not heal anyone; only God, the Almighty, the Majestic, heals. He said, Me? He said, No. He said, Do you have a lord other than me? He said, My Lord and your Lord is God. Then the king seized him again and continued torturing him until he directed him to the monk. Then the monk was brought and the king said, Return from your religion, but he refused. So the king placed the saw in the parting of his head until his sides fell off. He also said to the blind man, Return from your religion, but he refused. So the king placed the saw in the parting of his head until his sides fell off. The king said to the boy, Abandon your religion. He refused, so he sent him with some people to such-and-such a mountain and said, When you reach its peak, if he renounces his religion, well and good, roll him down from its top. So they took him, and when they had ascended the mountain, he said, O God, protect me from them however You wish. So the mountain shook and they were all rolled down. The boy came groping around until he entered upon the king. The king asked, What happened to your companions? He said, God has protected me from them. So he sent him with some people in a boat. He said, When you take him to the sea, if he renounces his religion, well and good, drown him in the sea. So they took him to the sea and the boy said, O God, protect me from them however You wish. So they were all drowned. The boy came until he entered upon the king. He said, What happened to your companions? He said, God sufficed me against them. Then he said to the king, "You will not kill me until you do what I command you. If you do what I command you, you will kill me. Otherwise, you will not be able to kill me." The king said, What is that? He said, "Gather the people in one plain, then crucify me on a tree-trunk and take an arrow from my quiver. Then say, 'In the name of God, Lord of the boy,' for if you do that, you will kill me." So he did and put the arrow to the bow of his bow and shot it, saying, In the name of God, Lord of the boy. The arrow struck his temple. The boy put his hand over the spot of the arrow and died. The people said, We believe in the Lord of the boy. The king was asked, Have you seen what you were fearing? By God, he has come to you and all people have believed. So he ordered that ditches be dug in the mouths of the streets and fires be set in them. He said: Whoever abandons his religion, let him go, otherwise throw him into it. He said: So they were competing in it and pushing each other. Then a woman came with her son to breastfeed, and it was as if she was reluctant to fall into the fire. The boy said: Be patient, O mother, for you are on the truth. And thus Muslim narrated it at the end of Sahih on the authority of Hadbah bin Khalid on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah with a similar chain of transmission. And al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Ahmad bin Salman on the authority of Affan on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah and through the chain of transmission of Hammad bin Zaid, both of them on the authority of Thabit with it, and they shortened the beginning of it. And Imam Abu ‘Isa al-Tirmidhi authenticated it as good, for he narrated it in the interpretation of this surah on the authority of Mahmud bin Ghailan and ‘Abd bin Hamid - the meaning is the same - they said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq informed us on the authority of Mu’ammar on the authority of Thabit al-Banani on the authority of ‘Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Layla on the authority of Suhaib who said: When the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) prayed the ‘Asr prayer, he would whisper. And whispering in some of their sayings is moving the lips as if he is speaking. So it was said to him, ‘O Messenger of God, when you pray the ‘Asr prayer, you whisper.’ He said: ‘A prophet among the prophets was amazed by his nation and said: Who will stand up for these people?’ So God revealed to him that he gave them the choice between me taking revenge on them and me unleashing their enemy upon them, so they chose revenge, so God unleashed death upon them, and seventy thousand of them died in one day.’ He said: And whenever he narrated this hadith, he narrated this other hadith. He said: There was a king who had a priest who used to divine for him. The priest said: “Find me a young man who is intelligent, or he said: One who is perceptive and knowledgeable, so I can teach him this knowledge of mine.” So he mentioned the whole story, and at the end of it he said: God Almighty says: “Those who were with the trench were the fire fueled, when they were sitting by it, and they were witnesses to what they were doing to the believers. They did not find fault with them except because they believed in God, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy.” He said: As for the boy, he was buried. It is mentioned that he was taken out during the time of Umar ibn al-Khattab, and his finger was on his temple as he had placed it when he was killed. Then al-Tirmidhi said: It is good and strange. This context does not explicitly state that the context of this story is from the words of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Our Sheikh, the hafiz Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi said: It is possible that it is from the words of Suhayb al-Rumi, for he had knowledge of the report of the Christians, and God knows best. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar mentioned this story in the biography in another context in which it contradicts what was mentioned above. He said: Yazid ibn Ziyad told me on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, and some of the people of Najran also told me on the authority of its people that the people of Najran were polytheists who worshipped idols. There was in one of its villages near Najran - and Najran is the largest village to which the people of that country gathered - a magician who taught the boys of Najran magic. When he settled there, they did not name him to me by the name that Ibn Munabbih named him. They said: A man settled there and built a tent between Najran and that village where the magician was, and the people of Najran began to send their boys to that magician to teach them magic. Then Al-Tamir sent his son Abdullah bin Al-Tamir with the young men of Najran. Whenever he passed by the owner of the tent, he was pleased with what he saw of his worship and prayer, so he would sit next to him and listen to him until he converted to Islam and believed in the Oneness of God and worshipped Him. He would ask him about the laws of Islam until he understood it and began to ask him about the Greatest Name. He had taught it to him but he concealed it from him and said to him: O my nephew, you will not be able to bear it. I fear that you will be weak in it. Al-Tamir Abu Abdullah thought that his son would go to the magician as young men go. When Abdullah saw that his companion was stingy with him and feared that he would be weak in it, he took cups and gathered them. Then he did not leave any name of God that he knew without writing it in a cup, for each name a cup. When he had counted them, he lit a fire and began to throw cups into it. When he passed by the Greatest Name, he threw his cup into it. The cup jumped until it came out of it without harming it. He took it and brought it to his companion and told him that he had learned the Greatest Name that he had written. The companion said: What is it? He said: It is such and such. He said: How did you know that? So he told him what he had done. He said: O my nephew, you have harmed him, so hold back. I do not think you will do that. So whenever Abdullah bin Al-Tamir entered Najran, he would not encounter anyone suffering from any harm except that he would say to him: O Abdullah, will you declare God’s oneness and enter into my religion, and will I pray to God for you to be cured of the affliction you are suffering from? He said, Yes. So he declared God’s oneness and submitted, and he prayed to God for him, and he was cured until there remained no one in Najran who was afflicted with any harm except that he came to him. So he followed his command and prayed for him, and he was cured until his matter was brought to the king of Najran, who summoned him and said to him, You have corrupted the people of my village and opposed my religion and the religion of my fathers, so I will mutilate you. He said, You are not able to do that. He said, “So he began to send him to the high mountain and throw him on his head, and he fell to the ground with no harm in him. And he began to send him to the waters of Najran, seas in which nothing is thrown but perishes, and he was thrown into them, and he came out with no harm in him. When he defeated him, Abdullah bin al-Tamir said to him, “By God, you will not be able to kill me until you believe in what I believe in and declare God’s oneness, for if you do, you will have power over me and kill me.” So that king declared God’s oneness and bore witness to the testimony of Abdullah bin al-Tamir, then he struck him with a stick in his hand and wounded him with a small wound, so he killed him. The king perished on the spot, and the people of Najran gathered around the religion of Abdullah bin al-Tamir, and he remained as he had come. Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, from the Gospel and his rule, then what happened to the people of their religion happened to them, so from there the origin of the Christian religion was in Najran. Ibn Ishaq said: This is the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ka`b al-Qurazi and some of the people of Najran on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Tamir, and God knows best which one it was. He said: So Dhu Nuwas marched towards them with his army and called them to Judaism and gave them the choice between that or death, and they chose death. So he dug the trench and burned it with fire and killed with the sword, and mutilated them until he killed nearly twenty thousand of them. So it was about Dhu Nuwas and his army that God Almighty revealed to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace: “The companions of the trench were destroyed. The fire fueled, when they were sitting by it, and they were witnesses to what they were doing to the believers. And they did not find fault with them for anything except that they believed in God, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy, to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And God is, over all things, Witness.” This is how Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned in the biography that the one who killed the companions of the trench was Dhu Nuwas, whose name was Zur`ah, and he was called Yusuf during his reign. He was the son of Bayan As`ad Abu Kurayb, who was Tubba’ who invaded Medina and covered the Ka`bah, and he took with him two rabbis from the Jews of Medina. So, some of the people of Yemen converted to Judaism at their hands, as Ibn In a single morning, Dhu Nuwas killed twenty thousand in the trench, and only one man, called Dos Dhu Tha’laban, escaped. He went as a horseman, and they pursued him but could not catch him. He went to Caesar, the king of Syria, who wrote to the Negus, the king of Abyssinia. He sent with him an army of Abyssinian Christians, led by Aryat and Abraha, and they rescued Yemen from the hands of the Jews. Dhu Nuwas fled, but he crossed the sea and drowned. The kingdom of Abyssinia remained in the hands of the Christians for seventy years. Then Saif bin Dhi Yazan Al-Himyari rescued him from the hands of the Christians when he sought help from Khosrau, the king of Persia. He sent with him those in the prisons, and they were close to seven hundred. He conquered Yemen with them, and the kingdom returned to Himyar. We will mention some of that, God willing, in the interpretation of Surah Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant? Ibn Ishaq said: Abdullah bin Abi Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazm told me that a man from Najran, during the time of Umar bin Al-Khattab, dug up a ruined area of Najran for some need. He found Abdullah bin Al-Tamir sitting under a burial place with his hand on a wound on his head, holding it with his hand. When he took his hand away from it, blood gushed out, and when he released his hand, it returned to it and held back its blood. On his hand was a ring on which was written, My Lord is God. He wrote to Umar bin Al-Khattab about it, informing him of his situation. Umar wrote to them to leave him as he was and to return him to the burial place he had been in, and they did so. Abu Bakr Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abi Al-Dunya, may God have mercy on him, said: Abu Bilal Al-Ash'ari told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ja'far bin Abi Talib, some of the people of knowledge told me that when Abu Musa conquered Isfahan, he found one of the walls of the city had fallen, so he built it, but it fell, then he built it, but it fell, and he was told: There is a righteous man under it, so he dug the foundation and found a man standing with a sword on which was written: I am Al-Harith bin Mudadh, I took revenge on the people of the trench, so Abu Musa extracted it and rebuilt the wall, and it stood firm. I said: He is Al-Harith bin Mudadh bin Amr bin Mudadh bin Amr Al-Jurhumi, one of the kings of Jurhum who were in charge of the Kaaba after the son of Thabit bin Ismail bin Ibrahim, and the son of this Al-Harith is Amr bin Al-Harith bin Mudadh, he was the last king of Jurhum in Mecca when Khuza'a expelled them and exiled them to Yemen, and he is the one who said in his poem, which Ibn Hisham said was the first poem recited by the Arabs: As if there was no companion between Al-Hujun and Al-Safa, and no one spent the evening in Mecca Yes, we were its people, but the vicissitudes of night and misfortune destroyed us. This implies that this story took place long ago, after the time of Ishmael, peace be upon him, by nearly five hundred years or so. What Ibn Ishaq mentioned implies that their story took place during the period between Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them both, which is more likely, and God knows best. It is possible that this happened many times in the world, as Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Al-Yaman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Jubayr, who said: The trench was in Yemen during the time of Tubba’ and in Constantinople during the time of Constantine when the Christians turned their qiblah away from the religion of Christ and monotheism, so they made a furnace and threw into it the Christians who followed the religion of Christ and monotheism. In Iraq, in the land of Babylon, there was Nebuchadnezzar, who made the idol and ordered the people to prostrate to it, but Daniel and his two companions, Azariah and Michael, refused, so he lit a furnace for them and threw wood and fire into it, then threw them into it. God made it cool and safe for them and saved them from it, but threw into it those who had transgressed against him, and they were nine men, and the fire consumed them. Asbat said on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding the Almighty’s statement: The companions of the trench were killed. He said: The trench was three: a trench in Iraq, a trench in Syria, and a trench in Yemen. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, and on the authority of Muqatil, he said: The trench was three: one in Najran in Yemen, another in Syria, and another in Persia. They were burned with fire. The one in Syria was Antoninus the Roman, the one in Persia was Bukhtanasr, and the one in the land of the Arabs was Yusuf Dhu Nuwas. As for the one in Persia and Syria, God Almighty did not send down a Qur’an regarding them, but He sent down the one in Najran. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Dashtaki told us, Abdullah ibn Abi Ja’far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabi’, who is Ibn Anas, regarding God Almighty’s statement: The companions of the trench were killed, he said: We heard that they were a people in a time of stagnation, and when they saw the tribulation and evil that had befallen the people and they became parties, each party rejoicing in what they had, they withdrew to a village and settled there and continued to worship God, devoting their religion to Him, being upright, and they established prayer and gave zakat. This was their situation until a tyrant heard about them and it happened. Their conversation, so he sent to them and ordered them to worship the idols they had taken, but they all refused him and said, We do not worship except God alone, with no partner for Him. So he said to them, If you do not worship these gods that I have worshipped, then I will fight you. But they refused him, so he made a trench of fire and the tyrant said to them and made them stand by it, Choose this or the one we are in. They said, This is more beloved to us. And among them were women and children. So the children were terrified and said to them, O my fathers, there is no fire after today. So they fell into it and their souls were taken before its heat touched them and the fire came out from its place and surrounded the tyrants, so God burned them with it. Concerning that, God, the Almighty, revealed: “The companions of the trench were destroyed. * The fire fueled * When they were sitting by it * And they were witnesses to what they were doing to the believers. * They did not blame them for anything except that they believed in God, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy * To whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And God is, over all things, Witness.” Ibn Jarir narrated it: I was told by Ammar, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Ja`far, with a similar narration. And the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, those who have persecuted the believing men and believing women meaning burned, as stated by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, and Ibn Abi Zayd, and then have not repented meaning they have not desisted from what they did and regretted what they did in the past, for them is the punishment of Hell, and for them is the punishment of the Burning Fire. This is because the recompense is of the same kind as the deed. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: Look at this generosity and benevolence. They killed His friends while He was calling them to repentance and forgiveness.
11:104: God Almighty says that in our destruction of the unbelievers and our salvation of the believers there is a sign that is, a lesson and a consideration of the truth of our promise in the afterlife. Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe during the worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses will stand. God Almighty also says, Then their Lord inspired to them, ‘We will surely destroy the wrongdoers.’ And His statement: That is a Day when mankind will be gathered together meaning the first and the last of them, like His statement: And We will gather them together and will not leave out a single one of them “And that is a witnessed Day” meaning a great Day in which the angels will attend and the messengers will gather and all of creation will be gathered from mankind, jinn, birds, beasts and animals, and the Just One will judge in it who will not wrong an atom’s weight, and if there is a good deed, He will multiply it. And His statement: And We do not delay it except for a specified term meaning We do not delay the establishment of the Resurrection except because the word of God preceded in the existence of a specified number of people from the descendants of Adam and He set a specific period, if it ends and the existence of those destined to emerge is complete, the Hour will come. For this reason He said: And We do not delay it except for a specified term meaning for a limited period that will not be increased or decreased. On the Day it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission meaning on the Day when the Day of Resurrection comes, no one will speak except by God’s permission, like His statement: They will not speak except he whom the Most Merciful permits and who says what is right and He said: And the voices will be hushed before the Most Merciful the verse. In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of intercession: “On that Day none will speak except the Messengers, and the call of the Messengers on that Day will be: ‘O God, save, save.’” And His statement: Among them are the wretched and the blessed, meaning that among the people of the gathering are the wretched and among them are the blessed, as He said: A group in Paradise and a group in the Blaze. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said in his Musnad: Musa ibn Hayyan told us, Abdul-Malik ibn Amr told us, Sulayman Abu Sufyan told us, Abdullah ibn Dinar told us, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of Umar, who said: When Among them are the wretched and the blessed, was revealed, I asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I said: O Messenger of God, what should we act upon? On something that has already been completed or on something that has not yet been completed? He said: On something that has already been completed, O Umar, and the pens have written about it, but each is facilitated for what he was created for. Then God, the Most High, explained the state of the wretched and the state of the blessed, saying:

11:106: The Almighty says, Therein they will have sighing and breathing. Ibn Abbas said, Sighing is in the throat and breathing is in the chest, meaning that their breathing is a sigh and their taking of the breath is a breathing, because of the torment they are in, may God protect us from that. They will abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure. Imam Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said: It is the custom of the Arabs, when they want to describe something as permanent, they say, This is permanent as long as the heavens and the earth endure. Likewise, they say, It remains as long as night and day differ, and The sons of Samir do not stay up late, and The camels do not flicker their tails, meaning by all of that, forever. So the Almighty addressed them with what they know among themselves, saying, They will abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure. I said: It is possible that what is meant by the heavens and the earth endure is the species, because in the Hereafter there must be heavens and earth, as God Almighty said, On the Day when the earth will be replaced by another earth, and the heavens will be replaced by another earth. For this reason, Al-Hasan Al-Basri said in his statement, As long as the heavens and the earth endure, he said, He means a heaven other than this heaven and an earth other than this, so what is that heaven and that earth endure? Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned on the authority of Sufyan bin Hussein on the authority of Al-Hakam on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: As long as the heavens and the earth endure, he said: For every paradise there is a heaven and an earth. And Abd al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: As long as the earth is an earth and the heaven is a heaven. And His saying, “Except what your Lord wills. Indeed, your Lord is the Doer of what He wills,” is like His saying, “The Fire is your abode, wherein you will abide eternally, except what God wills. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing.” The commentators differed regarding what is meant by this exception, with many statements narrated by Sheikh Abu al-Faraj Ibn al-Jawzi in his book Zad al-Masir, and other scholars of interpretation. Imam Abu Ja`far Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, transmitted many of them in his book, and he chose what he transmitted from Khalid Ibn Ma`dan, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, and Ibn Sinan. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan also, that the exception refers to the disobedient people of monotheism, whom God will bring out of the Fire through the intercession of the intercessors, from the angels, prophets, and believers, until they intercede for the people of major sins, then the mercy of the Most Merciful of the merciful comes and brings out from the Fire those who never did any good and said one day in their lives, There is no god but God, as was reported in the authentic and widespread reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the meaning of that from the hadith of Anas, Jabir, Abu Sa`id, Abu Hurayrah, and others from the Companions. And after that, no one will remain in the Fire except Whoever is obligated to abide therein eternally and has no escape from it, this is what many scholars, ancient and modern, have said in their interpretation of this noble verse. Its interpretation has been narrated on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Omar bin Al-Khattab, Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurairah, Abdullah bin Amr, Jabir, and Abu Saeed from the Companions, and on the authority of Abu Majlaz, Al-Shaabi, and others from the Followers, and on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam, Ishaq bin Rahawayh, and others from the Imams in strange sayings. A strange hadith was mentioned in Al-Tabarani’s Great Lexicon on the authority of Abu Umamah Siddi bin Ajlan Al-Bahili, but its chain of transmission is weak, and God knows best. Qatada said: God knows best about his two second terms. Al-Suddi said: It was abrogated by His statement, abiding therein forever.

11:108: God Almighty says: And as for those who are blessed, who are the followers of the Messengers, they will be in Paradise, meaning their abode is Paradise, abiding therein, meaning they will remain there forever, as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills. The meaning of the exception here is that their continuity in the bliss they are in is not something obligatory in and of itself, but rather it is entrusted to the will of God Almighty, so He is always to bestow His favor upon them, and for this reason they are inspired to glorify and praise Him just as they are inspired to breathe. Ad-Dahhak and Al-Hasan Al-Basri said that it is for the sinners among the monotheists who were in the Fire and then were taken out of it. He followed that with his saying, A gift that is not cut off, meaning not cut off. This was said by Mujahid, Ibn Abbas, Abu Al-Aaliyah and more than one person, so that no one would imagine, after mentioning the will, that there is an interruption or confusion or something. Rather, he made it inevitable for it to be permanent and not cut off, as he explained there, that the torment of the people of the Fire in the Fire is always returned to His will and that He tormented them with His justice and wisdom. For this reason, he said, Indeed, your Lord is the Doer of what He wills, as he said, He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned. Here, the hearts are pure and the intended meaning of his saying, A gift that is not cut off, is established. It was stated in the two Sahihs, “Death will be brought in the form of a white ram and slaughtered between Paradise and Hell, then it will be said, ‘O people of Paradise, eternity and no death, and O people of Hell, eternity and no death. ’” And in the Sahih also, “It will be said, ‘O people of Paradise, you will live and never die, you will be young and never grow old, you will be healthy and never fall ill, and you will enjoy and never be miserable. ’”
11:109: God the Almighty says: So be not in doubt about what these people worship the polytheists. It is falsehood, ignorance and misguidance. They only worship what their fathers worshipped before them. That is, they have no basis for what they are doing except following their fathers in ignorance. God will reward them for that with the most complete reward. He will punish their disbelievers with a punishment that He has not punished anyone else. Even if they have good deeds, God has already paid them back in this world before the Hereafter. Sufyan al-Thawri said on the authority of Jabir al-Ju'fi on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And We will surely pay them back their share, undiminished. He said: what they were promised of good or evil. And Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said, Those who will be given their share of the punishment will be given their full share, not diminished. Then the Almighty mentioned that He gave Moses the Book and people differed about it, so who would believe in it and who would disbelieve in it? So you have an example in those who came before you, O Muhammad, so do not be angered by their denial of you, nor will that concern you. And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them. Ibn Jarir said, Had it not been for what preceded of postponing the punishment to a known term, God would have judged between them. It is possible that what is meant by the word is that no one will be punished except after the proof has been established against him and the Messenger has been sent to him, as He said, And We never punish until We have sent a Messenger. For He said in another verse, “And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been binding and a specified term. So be patient over what they say.” Then the Almighty informed that He will gather the first and the last of the nations and reward them for their deeds, if good then good, and if evil then evil, so He said, “And indeed, your Lord will fully pay them their deeds. Indeed, He is Acquainted with what they do.” That is, He is All-Knowing of all their deeds, great and small, small and great, and in This verse has many readings, and its meaning goes back to what we mentioned, as in the Almighty’s saying: And indeed, all will be brought before Us.

He said: what they were promised of good or evil. And Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said, Those who will be given their share of the punishment will be given their full share, not diminished. Then the Almighty mentioned that He gave Moses the Book and people differed about it, so who would believe in it and who would disbelieve in it? So you have an example in those who came before you, O Muhammad, so do not be angered by their denial of you, nor will that concern you. And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them. Ibn Jarir said, Had it not been for what preceded of postponing the punishment to a known term, God would have judged between them. It is possible that what is meant by the word is that no one will be punished except after the proof has been established against him and the Messenger has been sent to him, as He said, And We never punish until We have sent a Messenger. For He said in another verse, “And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been binding and a specified term. So be patient over what they say.” Then the Almighty informed that He will gather the first and the last of the nations and reward them for their deeds, if good then good, and if evil then evil, so He said, “And indeed, your Lord will fully pay them their deeds. Indeed, He is Acquainted with what they do.” That is, He is All-Knowing of all their deeds, great and small, small and great, and in This verse has many readings, and its meaning goes back to what we mentioned, as in the Almighty’s saying: And indeed, all will be brought before Us.
11:112: God Almighty commands His Messenger and His believing servants to be steadfast and to continue on the right path, and that is the greatest aid to victory over enemies and opposing opponents. He forbade tyranny, which is oppression, for it is a fatal outcome, even if it is against a polytheist. God Almighty knows that He is All-Seeing of the deeds of His servants, and He does not neglect anything, and nothing is hidden from Him. And His statement: And do not incline toward those who do wrong. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Do not be complaisant. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It is inclining toward polytheism. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: Do not be satisfied with their deeds. Ibn Jarir said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And do not incline toward those who do wrong. This statement is good, meaning do not seek help from the oppressors, so that it is as if you have been satisfied with their deeds. Then the Fire will touch you, and you will have no protectors besides God; then you will not be helped. That is, you will have no protector besides Him to save you, nor any helper to deliver you from His punishment.

11:114: Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And establish prayer at the two ends of the day, he said, meaning the dawn and sunset prayers. This is what Al-Hasan and Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said. Al-Hasan said in the narration of Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak and others, it is the dawn and afternoon prayers. Mujahid said: it is the dawn prayer at the beginning of the day and the noon and afternoon prayers at the end of it. And at the approach of the night, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Hasan and others said, it means the evening prayer. Al-Hasan said in the narration of Ibn Al-Mubarak on the authority of Mubarak bin Fadala on his authority, And at the approach of the night, meaning the sunset and the evening prayers. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They are the two approaches of the night, the sunset and the evening prayers. This is what Mujahid, Muhammad bin Ka'b, Qatadah and Ad-Dahhak said, it is the sunset and evening prayers. It is possible that this verse was revealed before the five daily prayers were made obligatory on the Night of the Isra', because only two prayers were obligatory: a prayer before sunrise and a prayer before sunset, and during the night he and the nation stood up, then it was abrogated for the nation and its obligation was established for him, then it was abrogated for him also in a statement, and God knows best. And his saying: Indeed, good deeds remove bad deeds means that doing good deeds expiates past sins, as came in the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad and the people of the Sunnah on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: When I heard a hadith from the Messenger of God, God would benefit me with whatever He willed to benefit me from it, and if someone told me about it, I would make him swear, and if he swore to me, I would believe him. Abu Bakr told me, and Abu Bakr was truthful, that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: There is no Muslim who commits a sin and performs ablution and prays two rak’ahs except that he will be forgiven. And in the two Sahihs on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful Uthman ibn Affan, that he performed ablution for them like the ablution of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then he said: This is how I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution, and he said: Whoever performs ablution as I do, then prays two rak’ahs without thinking about it, his previous sins will be forgiven. And Imam Ahmad and Abu Ja’far ibn Jarir narrated from the hadith of Abu Aqil Zuhrah ibn Ma’bad that he heard Al-Harith, the freed slave of Uthman, say: Uthman sat down one day and we sat down with him, and the muezzin came to him and he called out. Uthman with water in a vessel, I think it would be about a mudd, so he performed ablution and then said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution as I do, then he said: “Whoever performs ablution as I do, then stands up and prays the noon prayer, his sins between that time and the dawn prayer will be forgiven. Then he prays the afternoon prayer, his sins between that time and the noon prayer will be forgiven. Then he prays the sunset prayer, his sins between that time and the afternoon prayer will be forgiven. Then he prays the night prayer, his sins between that time and the sunset prayer will be forgiven. Then he may spend the night wallowing in it, then if he stands up and performs ablution and prays the dawn prayer, his sins between that time and the night prayer will be forgiven. And good deeds eliminate bad deeds.” In Sahih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: Do you think that if there was a river at the door of one of you and he washed himself in it five times every day, would any dirt remain on him? They said: No, O Messenger of God. He said: Likewise, the five daily prayers, with which God wipes out sins and faults. Muslim said in his Sahih: Abu al-Tahir and Harun ibn Sa`id told us: Ibn Wahb told us on the authority of Abu Sakhr that `Umar ibn Ishaq, the freed slave of Zaydah, told him on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: The five daily prayers, and Friday to Friday, and Ramadan to Ramadan, are expiations for what is between them, as long as major sins are avoided. Imam Ahmad said: Al-Hakam ibn Nafi` told us: Ismail ibn `Ayyash told us on the authority of Damdam ibn Zur`ah on the authority of Shuraih ibn `Ubayd that Abarhum al-Sam`i used to narrate that Abu Ayyub al-Ansari told him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: Every prayer wipes out the sins that came before it. Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn `Auf told us: Muhammad ibn Ismail told us: My father told us on the authority of Damdam ibn Zur`ah on the authority of Shuraih ibn `Ubayd on the authority of Abu Malik al-Ash`ari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Prayers have been made expiations. “Because between them,” God said, Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. Al-Bukhari said: Qutaybah ibn Sa`id narrated to us, Yazid ibn Zari` narrated to us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, that a man kissed a woman, so he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him. Then God revealed, “And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds.” The man said, O Messenger of God, is this for me? He said, For all of my nation, all of them. This is how he narrated it in the Book of Prayer. He included it in the Tafsir on the authority of Musaddad on the authority of Yazid ibn Zari` in a similar manner. Muslim, Ahmad, and the people of the Sunan, except Abu Dawud, narrated it through various chains of narration on the authority of Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, whose name was Abd al-Rahman ibn Mal. It was narrated by Imam Ahmad, Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Jarir, and this is its wording, through various chains of transmission on the authority of Samak bin Harb, that he heard Ibrahim bin Yazid narrating on the authority of Alqamah and Al-Aswad on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: A man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I found a woman in a garden and I did everything to her except that I did not have intercourse with her. I kissed her and stuck to her and did nothing else, so do with me as you wish. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not say anything, so the man went away. Umar said: God had concealed him if he had concealed himself. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, followed him with his gaze and said: Bring him back to me. They brought him back to him and he recited to him: “Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.” Mu’adh said, and according to the narration of Umar: O Messenger of God, is it for him alone or for all of the people? He said: Rather, it is for all people. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ubayd told us, Aban ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of al-Sabah ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Murrah al-Hamadani, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God has divided your morals among you as He has divided your provisions among you. God gives the world to whom He loves and to whom He does not love, but He does not give religion except to whom He loves. So whoever God gives religion to, He loves him. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, a servant does not become Muslim until his heart and tongue become Muslim, and he does not believe until his neighbor is safe from his evil.” We said: What are his evils, O Prophet of God? He said: “He cheated him and oppressed him. No servant earns unlawful wealth and spends from it and it is blessed for him, nor does he give charity and it is accepted from him, nor does he leave it behind him except that it is his provision for the Fire. Indeed, God does not erase evil with evil, but He erases evil with good. Indeed, evil does not erase evil.” Ibn Jarir said: Abu al-Sa’ib told us, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: So-and-so ibn Mu’tab was a man from the Ansar and said: O Messenger of God, a woman entered upon me and I did with her what a man does with his wife except that I did not have intercourse with her. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not know how to answer him until this verse was revealed: “And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.” So the Messenger of God called him and recited it to him. Ibn Abbas said that he was Amr ibn Ghaziyah al-Ansari al-Tammar. Muqatil said that he was Abu Nufayl Amir ibn Qays al-Ansari. Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi mentioned that he was Abu al-Yusr Ka’b ibn Amr. Imam Ahmad said: Yunus and Affan told us: Hammad, meaning Ibn Salamah, told us on the authority of Ali Ibn Zaid. Affan said: Ali Ibn Yazid told us on the authority of Yusuf Ibn Mihran on the authority of Ibn Abbas that a man came to Umar and said: A woman came to pledge allegiance to him, so I entered her into the vagina and had intercourse with her without intercourse. He said: Woe to you, perhaps she was absent in the cause of God? He said: Yes. He said: Go to Abu Bakr and ask him. He said: So he went to him and asked him. He said: Perhaps she was absent in the cause of God? He said the same as Umar had said. Then he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said the same to him. He said: Perhaps she was absent in the cause of God. And the Qur’an was revealed: “And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds” to the end of the verse. He said: O Messenger of God, is it for me specifically or for all people? So he struck his chest with his hand and said, No, not even the blessing of the eye, but for the people in general. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Umar has spoken the truth. Imam Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir narrated from the hadith of Qays ibn al-Rabi` from Uthman ibn Muhab from Musa ibn Talhah from Abu al-Yusr Ka`b ibn Amr al-Ansari, who said, “A woman came to me to buy dates from me for a dirham. I said, ‘There are better dates in the house than these.’ So I entered and was drawn to her and kissed her. Then I went to Umar and asked him. He said, ‘Fear God and conceal yourself and do not tell anyone.’ I could not be patient until I went to Abu Bakr and asked him. He said, ‘Fear God and conceal yourself and do not tell anyone.’ I could not be patient until I went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him. He said, ‘You left behind a man fighting in the cause of God with his family like this.’ I thought I was one of the people of Hellfire and wished I had become Muslim at that moment. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, lowered his head for a moment and Gabriel came down. Abu al-Yusr said, ‘So I came and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited to me, “And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds are rewarded.” It removes evil deeds. This is a reminder for those who remember.” A man said: O Messenger of God, is it specifically for him or for all people? He said: For all people. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Hasan al-Daraqutni said: Al-Husayn ibn Ismail al-Muhammadi narrated to us: Yusuf ibn Musa narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us: Abd al-Malik ibn Umair narrated to us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla narrated to us: Muadh ibn Jabal said: He was sitting with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when a man came and said: O Messenger of God, what do you say about a man who has intercourse with a woman who is not permissible for him, and he did not leave anything that the man had intercourse with his wife without having intercourse with her? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Perform ablution well, then get up and pray. Then God, the Almighty, revealed this verse, meaning His statement: And establish prayer at the two ends of the day. Muadh said: Is it specifically for him or for all Muslims? He said: Rather, for all Muslims. Ibn Jarir narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Abd al-Malik ibn Umair. Abdul Razzaq said: Muhammad bin Muslim told us on the authority of Amr bin Dinar on the authority of Yahya bin Ja’dah that a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned a woman while he was sitting with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked his permission to enter for a need, and he gave him permission. He went to look for her but did not find her. The man came wanting to give the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, good report of rain, but he found the woman sitting by a pond. He pushed her chest and sat between her legs, and his penis became like a tuft of hair. He got up regretfully until he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him what he had done. He said to him: Seek forgiveness from your Lord and pray four rak’ahs. He said: And he recited to him: And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Ibn Jarir said: Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Sibawayh told me, Ishaq bin Ibrahim told us, Amr bin Al-Harith told us, Abdullah bin Salim told me, on the authority of Al-Zubaidi, on the authority of Salim bin Aamer, that he heard Abu Umamah say that a man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, uphold the limits of God - once or twice - so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away from him, then the prayer was called, and when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished praying, he said: Where is this man who says, ‘Uphold the limits of God’? He said: I am here. He said: Did you complete the ablution and pray with us just now? He said: Yes. He said: Then you will be as from your sins as on the day your mother bore you, so do not do it again. And God revealed to the Messenger of God: “And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.” Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, Ali bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Abu Uthman, who said: I was with Salman al-Farsi under a tree, and he took a dry branch from it and shook it until its leaves fell, then he said: Abu Uthman, will you not ask me why I did this? I said: Why did you do it? He said: This is what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did. He said: When a Muslim performs ablution and does it well, then prays the five daily prayers, his sins fall away like these leaves fall away. And he said: “And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.” Imam Ahmad said: Waki’ narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Thabit, on the authority of Maymun ibn Abi Shabib, on the authority of Muadh, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: O Muadh, Follow up a bad deed with a good one, which will erase it, and treat people with good character. Imam Ahmad said: Waki’ narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Maymun ibn Abi Shabib, on the authority of Abu Dharr, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Fear God wherever you may be, and follow up a bad deed with a good one, which will erase it, and treat people with good character. Ahmad said: Abu Mu’awiyah narrated to us, Al-A’mash narrated to us, on the authority of Shimr ibn ‘Atiyyah, on the authority of his sheikhs, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: I said: O Messenger of God, advise me. He said: If you do a bad deed, follow it up with a good one, which will erase it. I said: O Messenger of God, are the good deeds ‘There is no god but God’? He said: It is the best of good deeds. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili said: Hudhayl ibn Ibrahim al-Jumani told us, Uthman ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Zuhri told us, on the authority of the son of Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No servant says ‘There is no god but God’ at any hour of the night or day, but that whatever is in his record of bad deeds will be erased until it is replaced by an equal number of good deeds. Uthman ibn Abd al-Rahman is called al-Waqqasi, and he is weak. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Bishr ibn Adam and Zayd ibn Akram told us, they said: Ad-Dahhak ibn Mukhallad told us, Mastour ibn Abbad told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, that a man said: O Messenger of God, I have not left out any need or a chicken. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you bear witness that there is no god but God and that I am the Messenger of God? He said: Yes. He said: Then this will come after that. Mastour is the only one who narrated it from this source.
