Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ubayd told us, Aban ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of al-Sabah ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Murrah al-Hamadani, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God has divided your morals among you as He has divided your provisions among you. God gives the world to whom He loves and to whom He does not love, but He does not give religion except to whom He loves. So whoever God gives religion to, He loves him. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, a servant does not become Muslim until his heart and tongue become Muslim, and he does not believe until his neighbor is safe from his evil.” We said: What are his evils, O Prophet of God? He said: “He cheated him and oppressed him. No servant earns unlawful wealth and spends from it and it is blessed for him, nor does he give charity and it is accepted from him, nor does he leave it behind him except that it is his provision for the Fire. Indeed, God does not erase evil with evil, but He erases evil with good. Indeed, evil does not erase evil.” Ibn Jarir said: Abu al-Sa’ib told us, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: So-and-so ibn Mu’tab was a man from the Ansar and said: O Messenger of God, a woman entered upon me and I did with her what a man does with his wife except that I did not have intercourse with her. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not know how to answer him until this verse was revealed: “And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.” So the Messenger of God called him and recited it to him. Ibn Abbas said that he was Amr ibn Ghaziyah al-Ansari al-Tammar. Muqatil said that he was Abu Nufayl Amir ibn Qays al-Ansari. Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi mentioned that he was Abu al-Yusr Ka’b ibn Amr. Imam Ahmad said: Yunus and Affan told us: Hammad, meaning Ibn Salamah, told us on the authority of Ali Ibn Zaid. Affan said: Ali Ibn Yazid told us on the authority of Yusuf Ibn Mihran on the authority of Ibn Abbas that a man came to Umar and said: A woman came to pledge allegiance to him, so I entered her into the vagina and had intercourse with her without intercourse. He said: Woe to you, perhaps she was absent in the cause of God? He said: Yes. He said: Go to Abu Bakr and ask him. He said: So he went to him and asked him. He said: Perhaps she was absent in the cause of God? He said the same as Umar had said. Then he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said the same to him. He said: Perhaps she was absent in the cause of God. And the Qur’an was revealed: “And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds” to the end of the verse. He said: O Messenger of God, is it for me specifically or for all people? So he struck his chest with his hand and said, No, not even the blessing of the eye, but for the people in general. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Umar has spoken the truth. Imam Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir narrated from the hadith of Qays ibn al-Rabi` from Uthman ibn Muhab from Musa ibn Talhah from Abu al-Yusr Ka`b ibn Amr al-Ansari, who said, “A woman came to me to buy dates from me for a dirham. I said, ‘There are better dates in the house than these.’ So I entered and was drawn to her and kissed her. Then I went to Umar and asked him. He said, ‘Fear God and conceal yourself and do not tell anyone.’ I could not be patient until I went to Abu Bakr and asked him. He said, ‘Fear God and conceal yourself and do not tell anyone.’ I could not be patient until I went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him. He said, ‘You left behind a man fighting in the cause of God with his family like this.’ I thought I was one of the people of Hellfire and wished I had become Muslim at that moment. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, lowered his head for a moment and Gabriel came down. Abu al-Yusr said, ‘So I came and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited to me, “And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds are rewarded.” It removes evil deeds. This is a reminder for those who remember.” A man said: O Messenger of God, is it specifically for him or for all people? He said: For all people. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Hasan al-Daraqutni said: Al-Husayn ibn Ismail al-Muhammadi narrated to us: Yusuf ibn Musa narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us: Abd al-Malik ibn Umair narrated to us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla narrated to us: Muadh ibn Jabal said: He was sitting with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when a man came and said: O Messenger of God, what do you say about a man who has intercourse with a woman who is not permissible for him, and he did not leave anything that the man had intercourse with his wife without having intercourse with her? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Perform ablution well, then get up and pray. Then God, the Almighty, revealed this verse, meaning His statement: And establish prayer at the two ends of the day. Muadh said: Is it specifically for him or for all Muslims? He said: Rather, for all Muslims. Ibn Jarir narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Abd al-Malik ibn Umair. Abdul Razzaq said: Muhammad bin Muslim told us on the authority of Amr bin Dinar on the authority of Yahya bin Ja’dah that a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned a woman while he was sitting with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked his permission to enter for a need, and he gave him permission. He went to look for her but did not find her. The man came wanting to give the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, good report of rain, but he found the woman sitting by a pond. He pushed her chest and sat between her legs, and his penis became like a tuft of hair. He got up regretfully until he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him what he had done. He said to him: Seek forgiveness from your Lord and pray four rak’ahs. He said: And he recited to him: And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Ibn Jarir said: Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Sibawayh told me, Ishaq bin Ibrahim told us, Amr bin Al-Harith told us, Abdullah bin Salim told me, on the authority of Al-Zubaidi, on the authority of Salim bin Aamer, that he heard Abu Umamah say that a man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, uphold the limits of God - once or twice - so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away from him, then the prayer was called, and when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished praying, he said: Where is this man who says, ‘Uphold the limits of God’? He said: I am here. He said: Did you complete the ablution and pray with us just now? He said: Yes. He said: Then you will be as from your sins as on the day your mother bore you, so do not do it again. And God revealed to the Messenger of God: “And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.” Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, Ali bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Abu Uthman, who said: I was with Salman al-Farsi under a tree, and he took a dry branch from it and shook it until its leaves fell, then he said: Abu Uthman, will you not ask me why I did this? I said: Why did you do it? He said: This is what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did. He said: When a Muslim performs ablution and does it well, then prays the five daily prayers, his sins fall away like these leaves fall away. And he said: “And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.” Imam Ahmad said: Waki’ narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Thabit, on the authority of Maymun ibn Abi Shabib, on the authority of Muadh, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: O Muadh, Follow up a bad deed with a good one, which will erase it, and treat people with good character. Imam Ahmad said: Waki’ narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Maymun ibn Abi Shabib, on the authority of Abu Dharr, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Fear God wherever you may be, and follow up a bad deed with a good one, which will erase it, and treat people with good character. Ahmad said: Abu Mu’awiyah narrated to us, Al-A’mash narrated to us, on the authority of Shimr ibn ‘Atiyyah, on the authority of his sheikhs, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: I said: O Messenger of God, advise me. He said: If you do a bad deed, follow it up with a good one, which will erase it. I said: O Messenger of God, are the good deeds ‘There is no god but God’? He said: It is the best of good deeds. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili said: Hudhayl ibn Ibrahim al-Jumani told us, Uthman ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Zuhri told us, on the authority of the son of Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No servant says ‘There is no god but God’ at any hour of the night or day, but that whatever is in his record of bad deeds will be erased until it is replaced by an equal number of good deeds. Uthman ibn Abd al-Rahman is called al-Waqqasi, and he is weak. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Bishr ibn Adam and Zayd ibn Akram told us, they said: Ad-Dahhak ibn Mukhallad told us, Mastour ibn Abbad told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, that a man said: O Messenger of God, I have not left out any need or a chicken. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you bear witness that there is no god but God and that I am the Messenger of God? He said: Yes. He said: Then this will come after that. Mastour is the only one who narrated it from this source.
11:116: God the Almighty says: Why were there not among the past generations remnants of good people who would forbid the evils, wrongdoings, and corruption that used to occur among them on earth? His statement: Except a few means that there were few of them of this type, they were not many, and they are the ones whom God saved when His wrath and sudden punishment came. For this reason God the Almighty commanded this noble nation to have among them those who would enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, as God the Almighty said: “And let there be among you a group inviting to good, enjoining what is right, and forbidding what is wrong. Those are the successful ones.” And in the hadith: If people see wrongdoing and do not change it, God will soon punish them all. For this reason God the Almighty said: Why were there not among the generations before you those who had a remnant who would forbid corruption on earth, except a few of those We saved from among them? And His statement: And those who did wrong pursued that in which they were luxurious means that they continued in their sins and wrongdoings and did not pay attention to the denunciation of those people until the punishment came upon them suddenly. And they were criminals. Then the Almighty informed us that He did not destroy a village except that it was unjust to itself, and that He did not bring His wrath and punishment to a village until they were the unjust, as the Almighty said: And We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves. And He said: And your Lord is not unjust to His servants.

11:118: God Almighty tells us that He is able to make all people one nation of faith or disbelief, as God Almighty said: And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them together. And His statement: And they will not cease to differ * Except whom your Lord has mercy upon. That is, there will not cease to be differences among people in their religions, beliefs, sects, schools of thought, and opinions. Ikrimah said: Differing in guidance. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: Differing in provision, some of them making others dominate. The first is the well-known and correct view. And His saying: Except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy means except for those who are shown mercy from the followers of the Messengers who adhered to what they were commanded of in religion, and the Messengers of God informed them of it, and this continued to be their habit until the Prophet and the Seal of the Messengers and Prophets came, so they followed him and believed in him and supported him, and they won happiness in this world and the Hereafter because they are the saved group, as came in the hadith narrated in the Musnads and Sunans through chains of transmission that support each other: The Jews split into seventy-one sects, and the Christians split into seventy-two sects, and this nation will split into seventy-three sects, all of them in the Fire except one group. They said: And who are they, O Messenger of God? He said: What I and my companions are upon. Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak with this addition. Ata’ said: And they will not cease to differ, meaning the Jews, Christians, and Magians, Except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy, meaning the Hanafi school. Qatada said: The people of God’s mercy are the people of the community, even if their homes and bodies are divided, and the people of His disobedience are the people of a division, even if their homes are united. And their bodies, and His saying: And for that He created them Al-Hasan Al-Basri said in a narration from him and for differences He created them, and Makki bin Abi Talha said from Ibn Abbas: He created them into two groups as He said: And among them is the wretched and the happy and it was said that He created them for mercy. Ibn Wahb said: Muslim bin Khalid informed me from Ibn Abi Nujayh from Tawus: that two men disputed before him and they increased, so Tawus said: You have differed and increased, so one of the two men said: For that He created us, so Tawus said: You have lied, so he said: Did not God say: And they will not cease to differ * Except whom your Lord has mercy upon, and for that He created them He said: He did not create them to differ, but He created them for the group and mercy as Al-Hakam bin Abaan said from Ikrimah from Ibn Abbas, he said: He created them for mercy and did not create them for punishment, and so said Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak and Qatadah, and the meaning of this statement goes back to the saying of God the Almighty: And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me and it was said rather what is meant is that He created them for mercy and differences as Al-Hasan Al-Basri said in a narration from him in His saying: And they will not cease to differ * Except whom your Lord has mercy upon, and for that He created them He created them. He said: People differ in their religions, Except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy. So whoever your Lord has mercy upon is not different. So it was said to him: For that reason He created them. He said: He created these for His Paradise and created these for His Hellfire and created for His punishment. And so said Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah and Al-A’mash. And Ibn Wahb said: I asked Malik about the words of God Almighty: And they will not cease to differ * Except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy. He said: A group will be in Paradise and a group will be in the Blaze. Ibn Jarir and Abu Ubaid Al-Farra’ chose this statement. And from Malik in what we narrated from him of the interpretation: And for that reason He created them, he said: For mercy, and some people said: For difference. And His saying: “And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together.” The Almighty informs us that He has already decreed and determined, in His perfect knowledge and penetrating wisdom, that among those He has created are those who deserve Paradise and those who deserve Hell, and that Hell must be filled with these two heavy burdens, the jinn and the people. And He has the conclusive argument and perfect wisdom. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Paradise and Hell quarreled. Paradise said: Why do only the weak and worthless of people enter me? Hell said: I have been favored by the arrogant and the tyrannical. So God, the Almighty, said to Paradise: You are My mercy, with you I have mercy on whomever I will. And He said to Hell: You are My punishment, with you I take revenge on whomever I will. And each of you will have its fill. As for Paradise, there will continue to be surplus until God creates for it a creation to inhabit the surplus of Paradise. As for Hell, it will continue to say: Is there more? Until the Lord of Glory places His foot upon it, and it will say: Enough, enough, by Your glory.”

11:120: God the Almighty says: And all the report that We relate to you of the report of the messengers who came before you with their nations, and how they had arguments and disputes, and what the prophets endured of denial and harm, and how God aided His believing party and let down His disbelieving enemies. All of this is what We strengthen your heart, O Muhammad, so that you may have an example in those of your brothers from the messengers who have passed away. And His statement: And there has come to you in this truth meaning this surah, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and a group of the Salaf said, and on the authority of Al-Hasan in a narration from him and Qatadah in this world, and the correct view is in this surah that includes the stories of the prophets and how God saved them and the believers in them and destroyed the disbelievers, there have come to you in it true stories and true report and an admonition by which the disbelievers are deterred and a reminder by which the believers are reminded.
11:121: God Almighty says, commanding His Messenger to say to those who do not believe in what he brought from his Lord, as a threat: Work according to your position, meaning according to your way and method. We are working, meaning according to our way and method. And wait, we are waiting, meaning: “You will soon know who will have the final outcome of the home. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.” God fulfilled His promise to His Messenger, supported him, aided him, and made His word the highest and the word of those who disbelieved the lowest. And God is Exalted in Might and Wise.

11:123: God the Almighty informs us that He knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and that to Him is the return and the final destination. Every worker will be given his work on the Day of Judgment, for He is the Creator and the Commander. So God the Almighty commanded us to worship Him and put our trust in Him. He is sufficient for those who put their trust in Him and turn to Him. And His statement: And your Lord is not unaware of what you do means that what those who disbelieved in you, O Muhammad, are not hidden from Him. Rather, He is All-Knowing of their conditions and will reward them for that with the most perfect reward in this world and the Hereafter, and He will grant you and your party victory over them in both abodes. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee' told us, Zaid ibn Al-Habbab told us, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Abu Imran Al-Jawni, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Rabah, on the authority of Ka'b, who said: The conclusion of the Torah is the conclusion of Hud. The last interpretation of the surahs of Hud, peace be upon him. Praise and thanks be to God.
